meta.description: Machine-readable execution semantics for SAGE pipeline steps. This policy documents scheduling intent; it does not replace the dependency DAG.

dag_parallel_safe.description: May run in the reactive DAG executor once dependencies are satisfied. Parallel safety still requires disjoint writes and normal SQLite busy-timeout behavior.

sequential_required.description: Should run after dependency-bound producers because it reads broad/global state, writes final proof surfaces, or validates release artifacts.

full_run_only.description: Only meaningful during full/deep profiles; should not be triggered by a narrow watchdog pulse unless explicitly requested.

explicit_step_freshness.rationale: Explicit steps may reuse a dependency only when every declared output is current SQLite truth relative to the current Atlas anchor.

engine_progress.rationale: Long-running engines emit bounded start, phase, checkpoint, progress and completion telemetry. Time cadence is inherited from the central pipeline heartbeat; the high item threshold prevents fast file loops from becoming console noise.

heartbeat_cadence.claim_boundary: Local runtime telemetry selects only operator update cadence. It does not alter timeouts, scheduling, repository evidence, or release claims.
heartbeat_cadence.rationale: Fast and constrained machines receive bounded local cadence after enough same-scope observations. Until then, the safe bootstrap cadence remains explicit and observable.

pipeline_run_receipts.retry_rule: A transport timeout, stale heartbeat or unknown receipt never authorizes a duplicate run. Poll the same run_id and reconcile process state before retry.
pipeline_run_receipts.claim_boundary: A terminal PASS proves only that the recorded invocation returned successfully. It does not prove repository correctness, quality-gate success, finding validity or release readiness.
pipeline_run_receipts.rationale: One SQLite-first invocation identity survives a lost shell, IDE or agent transport and keeps acquisition, pipeline completion, evidence closeout, process-exit readiness and terminal state attributable without creating a second run ledger.

pipeline_lock.rationale: A stable endpoint plus an operating-system advisory lock prevents PID-reuse and unlink/recreate races. Metadata reports the holder but never authorizes eviction.

step_system_scope_policy.identity_rule: Repository acquisition mode does not determine the governance subject. Normal pipeline runs analyze a repository in both default-workspace and explicit-target acquisition modes; SAGE self-governance is entered only through an explicit self-governance surface.

shared_repository_analysis.rationale: These steps analyze or govern the selected repository subject. They may run when SAGE is the explicit self target or when an external target repository is selected.

sage_product_governance.rationale: These steps validate, release, package, or summarize the SAGE product itself. External target runs must not present their outputs as target-repository truth.

step_system_scope_policy.claim_boundary: System scope controls which subject a pipeline step may evaluate. It does not broaden language support, authorize mutation, or convert SAGE product release evidence into target-repository proof.

manual_validator_execution_policy.sqlite_writer_rule: release-proof steps with raw_artifact persistence are SQLite writers and must be serialized when dependency-linked or when more than one selected writer exists

subprocess_runtime_policy.default_rule: Long-running or captured child processes must use tools.core.subprocess_telemetry.run_observed_subprocess so waits, timeouts, and process-tree termination are observable and cross-platform.

protocol_surfaces.rule: Protocol-bound tools such as MCP may use the shared helper with log=null so stdout is not polluted while still preserving bounded timeout behavior.

tools/run_release_proof_bundle.py.rationale: Release proof streams child output and heartbeats directly because it is the top-level proof runner.

tools/orchestrators/watchdog.py:auto_ref.rationale: Watchdog auto-refresh announces command, timeout, result, and honesty telemetry; child output is intentionally operator-visible.

tools/core/bootstrap_env.py:run_command.rationale: Bootstrap setup should let dependency tools speak directly while remaining bounded by central operational_limits.

tools/orchestrators/watchdog.py:git_rest.rationale: Circuit-breaker restore is gated by HITL policy, bounded by watchdog_git_restore_timeout_seconds, and records honesty telemetry on timeout.

tools/core/bootstrap_env.py:version_chec.rationale: Python and Node version probes are bounded by bootstrap_command_timeout_seconds and only produce pass/warn setup status.

tools/tests.rationale: Tests may invoke subprocesses to exercise CLI behavior and patch runtime subprocess calls.

entrypoint_failure_drills.rationale: Entrypoint failure drills run six sequential observed subprocess checks, including the bounded dead-code failure drill. The outer release-proof runner must reserve their declared combined limit plus policy headroom.

operational_parity_full_validation.rationale: Operational parity performs lifecycle validation before and after a cached full-pipeline replay. The outer release-proof runner must reserve the declared sequential inner budget plus policy headroom; workload adaptation may only extend this floor.

installation_proof_smoke.rationale: Installation proof smoke runs five sequential observed subprocess checks. The release-proof outer runner must reserve their centrally declared combined limit plus policy headroom.

release_analysis_quality_gate_refresh.rationale: Release proof refreshes the bounded forced daily MAIN producer set before runtime-artifact consumers run. This step establishes representative repository evidence but does not claim that final governance was evaluated. The outer runner derives policy headroom from the central pipeline limit.

release_quality_gate_refresh.rationale: Release proof evaluates the explicit MAIN Quality Gates closure over the fresh bounded-analysis evidence produced by its direct dependency and requires quality_gate.json to be rewritten during the step. It does not rebuild Atlas a second time. Target findings remain evidence rather than SAGE product-process failure.

installation_preflight.claim_boundary: Local duration guidance is advisory wait information for target inspection only. It does not change timeout, dependency, repository, analysis or release semantics.
installation_preflight.rationale: Target-aware installation planning can inspect large repository topology before it knows which dependencies apply; exact local samples provide honest wait guidance without fixed machine assumptions.

operational_parity.claim_boundary: Local duration guidance is advisory wait information only. It does not alter timeout floors, semantic freshness, release readiness or repository truth.
operational_parity.rationale: Operational parity has three sequential subprocess phases. Exact identifiers prevent a lifecycle-only sample from being presented as a completed replay estimate.

cli_long_running_timeout_none.rationale: Run, watch, MCP server, and list-step command surfaces intentionally delegate lifetime control to the operator or child pipeline; bounded subprocess steps use operational_limits instead.

discovery_workspace_bfs_max_depth.rationale: Workspace discovery uses a shallow local BFS to find nearby project roots without scanning whole user directories; broader explicit targets should use --target-root or project registry configuration.

orchestrator_reactive_poll_interval.rationale: The reactive DAG loop uses a short local wait interval for responsiveness while child step timeouts and execution policy are governed separately.

validation_governance_red_lines.purpose: Prevent validation sprawl while preserving SAGE's claim -> evidence -> validation -> human seal discipline.

rules.rule: A new validator or smoke test must protect a release claim, a known edge-case, a precondition boundary, or a user/agent safety surface.
Do not add another validator for an already-covered behavior unless it detects a distinct false-green or false-red failure mode.
Clean source package checks must not require generated analysis artifacts; post-analysis validators must fail closed when required artifacts are absent.
Watchdog/save-time loops may record proof debt and narrow governance signals, but must not silently run heavyweight release-deep proof.
Managed raw artifacts are SQLite-first; JSON shadows are compatibility exports or recovery fallback, not the primary truth source.

Agent-facing default work queues and edit directives are MAIN-first; variation, companion, and all-project scopes may appear only for merge/diff/proof workflows or explicit operator-selected all-project inspection.

Operational constants that change execution behavior, including timeouts, profile boundaries, project scopes, release claim boundaries, and agent packet budgets, must come from a central policy/config/helper or declare a scoped rationale; engine-local literals are allowed only for display text or non-behavioral labels.
When a defect reveals a reusable failure pattern, do not stop at the local fix; scan related surfaces for the same failure family and either fix, validate, or record a scoped non-blocking rationale.

project_scope_policy.purpose: Keep target-repository agent work MAIN-first while preserving explicit comparative/merge/proof use of variations and companion projects.
project_scope_policy.agent_surface_rule: Do not include variation or companion project edit directives in default target-repo agent packets; include them only as read-only comparative evidence unless the operator explicitly selects that project scope.
project_scope_policy.pipeline_rule: Full/release analysis may compute all registered projects for proof, but watchdog/daily/agent work queues should expose MAIN/host scope unless a merge, diff, corpus, or explicit all-project task is active.

source_clean.description: Can run in a clean source distribution before repository analysis artifacts are generated.

post_analysis.description: Requires a completed analysis run and current target-repository artifacts.

release_deep.description: Requires release/deep proof artifacts and should not be used as a cheap clean-source smoke.

external_target.description: Requires isolated output/external_targets artifacts for the exact target_root.

validate_agent_context_payloads.clean_mirror_rule: Do not run as clean-source proof before analysis artifacts exist.

validate_agent_semantic_contract_smoke.clean_mirror_rule: Run only after the clean mirror has completed analysis, not immediately after source sync.

validate_agent_packet_chain_integrity.clean_mirror_rule: Run only after analysis and agent surface inputs exist; do not use as a clean-source mirror validation.

validate_watchdog_snapshot_freshness.clean_mirror_rule: Run only after Atlas/source snapshots exist; do not use as a clean-source mirror validation.

generate_agent_surface_quality_review.clean_mirror_rule: Run only after analysis and agent surface inputs exist; do not use as a clean-source mirror validation.

validate_agent_surface_snippet_ranges.clean_mirror_rule: Run only after agent surface quality review artifacts exist; do not use as a clean-source mirror validation.

validate_agent_surface_source_grounding.clean_mirror_rule: Run only after agent surface quality review artifacts exist; do not use as a clean-source mirror validation.

validate_step_isolation.clean_mirror_rule: Do not run as clean-source proof; it executes pipeline steps and intentionally writes analysis artifacts.

validate_operational_parity.clean_mirror_rule: Do not run as clean-source proof; it refreshes quality gates and cached full pipeline semantic snapshots.

release-deep.description: Complete release proof profile. Runs heavyweight validation and merge intelligence.

deep.description: Alias of release-deep for deep validation runs.

full.description: Normal full analysis. Honors step-level release_deep_only gates.

daily.description: Fast dependency-closed development profile. Refreshes core repository truth, bounded quality signals and ContextOS evidence without claiming a final governance verdict.

dna_unchanged_fast_path.description: Minimal no-op pulse when changed files do not alter Project DNA.

absolute_zero.description: Minimal status/report pulse when no changed files are detected.

watchdog_surgical_gate.description: Narrow save-time gate before live/smoke watchdog behavior removes policy-heavy steps.

state_flow_signal_sensitive.description: Steps removed from live watchdog pulses when changed files carry no state-flow signals.

state_flow.description: Keep state-flow analysis only when changed Atlas nodes carry state-management or client-action evidence.

first_repo_onboarding.purpose: Initial repository entry. Establish Discovery, Atlas, Project DNA, Architecture Oracle proposal, doctrine inputs, and baseline reports before narrow governance claims are trusted.
first_repo_onboarding.trigger: sage init, codemaps init, first full run, or a target root with missing/stale atlas_commit
first_repo_onboarding.ssot_expectation: Atlas and SQLite state_payloads may be empty at start; run truth producers before downstream governance.
first_repo_onboarding.agent_surface: Return onboarding status, missing setup actions, proposed doctrine, and claim boundaries. Do not present release readiness as sealed proof.

normal_full.purpose: Normal complete local analysis after onboarding. Refreshes current structural truth and broad governance artifacts without forcing every release-deep proof drill.
normal_full.ssot_expectation: Atlas/SQLite state should be current or regenerated for stale projects before downstream engines run.
normal_full.agent_surface: Return current architecture facts, risks, quality gates, and relevant capabilities. Mark heavyweight release-only evidence as absent unless release-deep ran.

daily.purpose: Fast dependency-closed development loop. Refresh core repository truth, React applicability and bounded agent context while leaving final governance to a complete producer closure.
daily.trigger: codemaps run --profile daily or local development check
daily.ssot_expectation: Use existing Atlas/SQLite as baseline and refresh stale truth producers selected by the daily profile.
daily.agent_surface: Return fresh daily spine status, skipped heavyweight steps, governance=NOT_EVALUATED, and whether full or release-deep proof is still needed.

watchdog_save_pulse.purpose: Narrow save-event pulse. Normalize changed files, refresh only affected truth surfaces, then distill ContextOS signals for the agent.
watchdog_save_pulse.ssot_expectation: Changed files must be normalized to PROJECT::relative nodes and written back to Atlas/SQLite before ContextOS packaging.
watchdog_save_pulse.agent_surface: Return only relevant files, affected symbols, reasons, capability hints, and explicit stale/deep-proof warnings.

auto_refresh.agent_rule: Automatic watchdog debt refresh is disabled by default. Enable auto_daily or auto_full for managed development loops; enable auto_release_deep only when the operator accepts heavyweight proof cost.

pulse_ledger.agent_rule: Latest watchdog_session may be overwritten by a later pulse, but unresolved pulse findings must remain queryable in the bounded ledger until they are resolved or explicitly acknowledged by a future surface.

deep_proof_debt_policy.agent_rule: Watchdog is a live constitutional guard and ContextOS signal loop. It must not be treated as full target-repository proof when repo-wide artifacts have been skipped or allowed to age.

release_deep.purpose: Release sealing profile. Runs complete proof, validation, claim guard, fixture/corpus, agent-surface, and distribution hardening checks.
release_deep.trigger: codemaps run --profile release-deep, codemaps run --full --force, or run_release_proof_bundle
release_deep.ssot_expectation: All required artifacts must be current, SQLite-backed, schema-valid, and included in release proof snapshots.
release_deep.agent_surface: Return release proof status, allowed claim, failed required steps, and evidence bundle pointers.

explicit_step.purpose: Operator-requested single step or from-step run. Honors the requested scope and does not imply global freshness unless upstream dependencies were also refreshed.
explicit_step.ssot_expectation: Requested step may read existing Atlas/SQLite; caller must inspect input artifact freshness when using the result as proof.
explicit_step.agent_surface: Return the step output, its declared inputs, stale-risk warning, and suggested follow-up validators.

external_corpus_validation.purpose: External repository validation/corpus evidence. Measures behavior-family coverage, false positives, false negatives, and fixture promotion candidates.
external_corpus_validation.trigger: external repo corpus run or manual validation batch
external_corpus_validation.ssot_expectation: External target facts must be isolated by target root/project identity and not overwrite the host workspace truth without explicit selection.
external_corpus_validation.agent_surface: Return category coverage, sampled manual findings, false-positive/false-negative notes, and fixture promotion candidates.

clean_install_onboarding_proof.purpose: Fresh machine/distribution proof. Verifies the package can initialize, run, validate, and expose agent surfaces from a clean copy.
clean_install_onboarding_proof.trigger: clean distribution mirror, friend machine proof, or final release candidate check
clean_install_onboarding_proof.ssot_expectation: Generated/cache artifacts may be absent at start; required setup and proof artifacts must be created by documented commands.
clean_install_onboarding_proof.agent_surface: Return install friction, missing dependency guidance, exact command transcript needs, and final release-proof status.

explicit_step_closure_policy.description: Central policy for operator-requested `run --step` commands. A step command runs the transitive dependency closure by default; broad/global closures must be visible before humans or agents treat the result as narrow evidence.

narrow.operator_warning: This step has a small dependency closure; it is suitable for targeted refresh when the listed inputs are current.

broad.operator_warning: This step has a broad dependency closure. Treat it as a partial pipeline refresh, not a cheap single-engine probe.

global.operator_warning: This step has a global dependency closure and may run most of the pipeline. Use a profile or a more specific agent-facing/MCP surface when you need surgical context.

aicontextgenerator.recommended_alternative: Use ContextOS/MCP surgical packet tools or `python sage.py run --profile daily` for narrow agent context. Reserve AI Context Generator for global index refresh.
aicontextgenerator.operator_warning: AI Context Generator reads global pipeline state and depends on most finalizers; it is not a cheap surgical context refresh.

artifactcontractvalidation.recommended_alternative: Use the specific artifact validator for a local contract check; reserve this step for broad artifact proof.

masterreportgeneration.recommended_alternative: Use release readiness, quality gate, or targeted reports for local evidence; reserve master report generation for human-facing summary refresh.

releasereadiness.recommended_alternative: Use quality gates for local verdicts; reserve release readiness for release envelope refresh.

nexoraoperatorpacket.recommended_alternative: Use MCP agent packet tools for narrow target-repo work; reserve operator packet refresh for current operator summary.

sequential_required_slugs.frameworkrouteanalyzer: contention-sensitive route graph expansion; isolated execution prevents CPU/IO inflation during full analysis
sequential_required_slugs.deadcodedetector: contention-sensitive public-contract scan; isolated execution prevents false performance regression under concurrent heavy analyzers
sequential_required_slugs.artifactcontractvalidation: validates broad artifact state and should see producers after writes settle
sequential_required_slugs.masterreportgeneration: aggregates many upstream reports into human-facing release context
sequential_required_slugs.nexoraoperatorpacket: packages current governance and ContextOS state for agent-facing use
sequential_required_slugs.aicontextgenerator: packages final agent context and reads broad pipeline state
sequential_required_slugs.releasereadiness: final release verdict over quality and merge surfaces
sequential_required_slugs.qualitygates: final quality gate over upstream proofs
sequential_required_slugs.proofobligations: proof synthesis over multiple upstream analysis outputs
sequential_required_slugs.contextosquantengine: packages active signals after dependency and audit outputs exist

full_run_sequential_slugs.oraclevalidationgate: validates generated merge scripts and sandbox outputs
full_run_sequential_slugs.blastradiusengine: expands graph impact over global dependency state
full_run_sequential_slugs.automerge_scriptgenerator: generates mutation plans and should not overlap with final validators

static_runtime_boundary_contract.claim_boundary: A runtime-oriented step covered by this contract analyzes repository evidence only. It does not claim target execution or runtime stderr authority.

keywordstats.rationale: Keyword stats are derived from Atlas/Genome and should reuse keyword_scanner_cache_meta when the Atlas snapshot and Genome payload are unchanged.

keywordscanner.rationale: Keyword scanning should be full/release evidence, not a save-pulse cost; unchanged Atlas/Genome signatures must hit the cache.

gemscorer.rationale: Gem scoring closes the keyword cache bundle and must publish keyword_scanner_cache_meta so later runs avoid rescanning unchanged project evidence.

variationengine.rationale: Cross-variation semantic alignment is valuable but expensive; daily runs should consume the latest existing variation artifact and refresh this step only during full/release proof or explicit operator requests.

hostmergeintelligence.rationale: Host-aware merge analysis reads broad merge/fractal surfaces; daily runs should consume existing merge evidence and refresh this step during full/release proof or explicit merge work.

oraclevalidationgate.rationale: Validation Oracle materializes compiler sandboxes and must run only during release-deep/deep proof or explicit operator requests.

mergedependencypackager.rationale: Merge dependency packaging is Atlas-backed but materializes transfer manifests; daily/watchdog should consume existing packages unless an explicit merge workflow is requested.

mergesimulationengine.rationale: Merge simulation depends on generated package manifests and should run in full/release or explicit merge workflows, not routine save pulses.

mergedecisioncockpit.rationale: Merge decision cockpit synthesizes merge evidence for humans/agents and should not imply fresh merge readiness during daily/watchdog profiles; consume existing cockpit evidence unless explicit merge proof is requested.

aitaskpackgenerator.rationale: AI merge task packs are derived from merge cockpit evidence; generate them only when merge evidence has been explicitly refreshed.

mergeintelligenceregression.rationale: Merge regression validates the merge-intelligence chain and belongs to full/release or explicit merge proof runs.

scopedhostanalyzer.rationale: Scoped host analysis is explicit-scope merge intelligence; run it only with an operator-provided scope or full/release merge work.

reactecosystemanalyzer.rationale: Deep React ecosystem synthesis is claim-critical for release proof but too broad for every watchdog pulse; refresh explicitly in full/release proof or targeted React claim work.

reactsupportmatrix.rationale: React support visibility is part of the daily governance spine, but it evaluates workspace- and project-wide capability evidence and must not run on every save pulse. Watchdog records the broad proof debt; daily/full profiles refresh the matrix.

reactcapabilityprobe.rationale: React capability discovery is package/discovery-wide onboarding evidence. Live source saves consume the existing capability truth and defer refresh to daily/full or explicit manifest work.

fractalmapping.rationale: Fractal genome analysis is broad topology work; daily profile should consume existing outputs unless explicitly refreshed.

entrypointfailuredrills.rationale: Entry-point failure drills protect install/onboarding and release surfaces but are not repository-analysis evidence. Installation proof invokes its own bounded health checks; full/release or explicit validation owns the complete drill family.

nuclearsequencing.rationale: Genome extraction is a truth-layer dependency; optimization must preserve Atlas/Genome integrity and incremental scope.

blastradiusengine.rationale: Daily refresh already updates Circular Dependency evidence consumed by Blast Radius, ContextOS and agent risk surfaces. Keeping the bounded project-scoped Blast Radius producer closes that freshness chain without enabling comparative merge or multi-project release work.

uiruntimecontractanalyzer.rationale: UI runtime contracts are useful for merge and smoke surfaces but should remain downstream of route/UI changes; refresh explicitly in full/release proof or targeted UI/runtime work.

artifactcontractvalidation.rationale: Artifact validation is a broad release safety net. Daily analysis validates its selected producers locally and leaves the complete artifact family contract to full/release or explicit validation.

qualitygates.rationale: Quality Gates are final governance verdicts and require the complete declared producer closure. Daily runs expose bounded signals and report governance as NOT_EVALUATED; full/release or explicit Quality Gate execution owns the verdict.

reactruntimeintelligence.rationale: Runtime intelligence is broad static React synthesis, does not execute the target or ingest test stderr, and should not run on every save pulse without explicit deep/release intent.

reactcompilerreadiness.rationale: Compiler readiness aggregates React runtime surfaces and belongs to explicit full or release proof flows.

reactfrontierintelligence.rationale: Frontier intelligence tracks broad React edge-case posture and should remain outside live save pulses; refresh explicitly during full/release claim validation.

healthscore.rationale: Health Score requires the complete declared keyword and structural evidence chain. Daily runs must not convert an intentionally omitted producer into a numeric zero; full/release or explicit execution owns the score.

proofobligations.rationale: Proof synthesis requires its complete producer closure, including release-deep Oracle evidence when applicable. Daily runs preserve proof debt and defer synthesis to full/release or explicit execution.

qualityrevieworacle.rationale: Review verdicts depend on upstream health, React, Oracle and proof surfaces. Daily runs must not score omitted evidence as zero; full/release or explicit execution owns the review.

aicontextgenerator.rationale: Full AI context generation is superseded by ContextOS surgical packets during live save pulses.

uimapper.rationale: UI mapping is the declared producer for the daily Framework Route Analyzer. It remains outside live save pulses but is refreshed in the dependency-closed daily profile.

projectdnaprofile.rationale: Project DNA is the authoritative capability and framework applicability producer for daily React and repository-scope analysis. Omitting it can turn missing evidence into a false NOT_APPLICABLE result.

ssot_optimization_plan.rationale: SSOT optimization planning scans runtime references across SAGE source trees. It is useful release/report evidence, but too broad for watchdog save pulses.

external_input_artifacts.description: Inputs consumed by pipeline steps that are not produced as managed raw artifacts by SAGE. Connectivity validators must classify these as external/runtime inputs, not missing producers.

architecture_doctrine.rationale: Architecture doctrine is human-sealed governance configuration consumed by analysis/reporting steps, not produced by a pipeline writer.

capability_activation_plan.rationale: Capability activation plan is generated by capability tooling outside the orchestrator step catalog, carries exact-project effective architecture policy context, preserves policy producers/internal consumers during scheduler filtering, and is projected into bounded operator/agent context.

capability_registry.rationale: Capability registry is central configuration consumed through capability helpers, not produced by a pipeline writer.

codemaps_adapters.rationale: Adapter declarations are configuration inputs consumed before adapter_registry is produced as a managed SAGE artifact.

codemaps_suppressions.rationale: Suppression declarations are governance configuration inputs consumed by release readiness, not produced by a pipeline writer.

discovery.rationale: Discovery configuration and workspace signals seed analysis before managed artifacts exist.

external_target_preflight.rationale: External-target preflight is produced by the acquisition boundary before the orchestrator pipeline and constrains the shared post-Atlas analysis scope authority.

atlas_bound_source.source: target repository source files bounded by Atlas scope and source_evidence guards
atlas_bound_source.rationale: Atlas-bound source evidence is live target source content used by migration-candidate analyzers, not a shadow JSON artifact produced by a prior pipeline writer.

package_json.rationale: Framework/package signals are read from the target repository, not produced by a SAGE artifact writer.

mcp_agent_surface_validation.rationale: MCP agent surface validation is produced by release-proof validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by release readiness as proof evidence.

engine_signal_contract_validation.rationale: Engine signal contract validation is produced by release-proof validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by operator packets as proof evidence.

hitl_approval_ledger.rationale: HITL approval ledger is maintained by governance/HITL tooling and consumed by operator packets, not produced by the static pipeline catalog.

hitl_decision_requests.rationale: HITL decision requests are maintained by governance/HITL tooling and consumed by operator packets, not produced by the static pipeline catalog.

hitl_governance_validation.rationale: HITL governance validation is produced by release-proof validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by operator packets as proof evidence.

hitl_lifecycle_smoke.rationale: HITL lifecycle smoke is produced by release-proof validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by operator packets as proof evidence.

nexora_agent_contract.rationale: Nexora agent contract is generated by agent-surface tooling outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by operator packets.

nexora_agent_handoff.rationale: Nexora agent handoff is an agent-surface runtime artifact consumed by operator packets, not a pipeline writer output.

nexora_agent_response_ledger.rationale: Nexora agent response ledger is an agent-surface runtime artifact consumed by operator packets, not a pipeline writer output.

nexora_agent_response_validation.rationale: Nexora agent response validation is produced by agent-surface validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by operator packets.

nexora_brief.rationale: Nexora brief is generated by agent-surface tooling outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by operator packets.

nexora_surface_inventory.rationale: Nexora surface inventory is generated after the operator packet and read by the MCP get_surface_inventory surface outside the orchestrator catalog. The operator packet links to the later inventory but does not consume its payload as evidence.

operational_parity_validation.rationale: Operational parity validation is produced by release-proof validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by release readiness as proof evidence.

performance_budget_validation.rationale: Performance budget validation is produced by release-proof validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by release readiness as optional proof evidence.

performance_ledger.rationale: Performance ledger is maintained by performance validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by release readiness as optional proof evidence.

pipeline_execution_contract_validation.rationale: Pipeline execution contract validation is produced by release-proof validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by operator packets as proof evidence.

react_fixture_matrix_validation.rationale: React fixture matrix validation is produced by release-proof validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by release readiness as proof evidence.

react_universal_readiness.rationale: React universal readiness is produced by release-proof validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by release readiness as claim evidence.

release_identity.rationale: Release identity is version/claim configuration consumed by release readiness and claim guard, not produced by a pipeline writer.

release_proof_bundle.rationale: Release proof bundle is produced by the release-proof runner outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by post-proof release surfaces. Pipeline generators must not read the final bundle before the proof run produces it.

report_freshness_index.rationale: Report freshness index is produced by release-proof/report validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by operator packets.

source_snapshot_store.source: SQLite source_snapshots table projected from Atlas file scope
source_snapshot_store.rationale: SQLite source snapshots are a runtime source-content store populated during Atlas/artifact persistence, not a managed raw JSON artifact with a single pipeline writer.

ts_diagnostics.source: TypeScript diagnostics collector output generated inside React Frontier Intelligence
ts_diagnostics.rationale: React Frontier invokes the local TypeScript diagnostics collector and reads its output as runtime evidence within the same step, so connectivity checks should not expect an upstream SAGE pipeline writer.

telemetry_traces.rationale: Telemetry traces are runtime observations consumed by local telemetry analysis rather than managed artifacts produced by an upstream pipeline step.

universal_proof_validation.rationale: Universal proof validation is produced by release-proof validators outside the orchestrator step catalog and consumed by release readiness as proof evidence.

watchdog_session.rationale: Live save-time sessions are runtime inputs that seed ContextOS signals.

ai_context_generator_policy.agent_rule: AI Context is a broad index of the authority-bound analyzed scope, not necessarily the whole repository. Do not use it alone as permission to edit; request a bounded ContextOS/MCP surgical packet before target-repository mutation.

product_governance_enrichment.claim_boundary: Target-repository AI Context must not inherit stale or unrelated SAGE product release, distribution, operator, MCP-readiness or performance evidence. Those surfaces remain available through explicit SAGE operator tools.

recommended_followups.reason: Use when the blast radius is the next decision point.
Use before choosing validation commands for a targeted patch.
Use when a finding needs upstream dependency evidence before editing.

decision_rules.mutation: Do not mutate from AI Context alone; obtain a target-repository surgical packet with file, symbol/span, evidence and validation contract.
decision_rules.human_approval: Ask for explicit human approval before mutation, merge/import, deletion, movement, public API change, or large refactor actions.
decision_rules.scope: Prefer MAIN scope for target-repository coding unless a merge/variation surface explicitly asks otherwise.
decision_rules.validation: Run packet-listed validators first; if none are listed, use the closest focused target-repository validator.
